prompt:
Edit the attached approved AdaptOps pitch slide reference into the corrected Physical Impact slide. The user explicitly wants THIS original composition and full product vision restored. Preserve its sophisticated white/navy/petrol/mint design, generous whitespace, two-column hierarchy, LARGE prepared COMPANY BRIEF, and complete five-step adaptation cycle surrounding it. Do not simplify the full product into a headless agent. Do not use the previous Physical Impact redesign as reference. The supplied original is the authority. One flat 16:9 pitch slide image, same approximately 1672x941 dimensions and typography proportions. All copy English, perfectly spelled, no clipped lines. No slide variant badge.

MAKE THESE THREE COHERENT REFINEMENTS:

1. BRAND AND LEFT PROMISE.
Replace AdaptOps with "Physical Impact", retaining one small mint mark. There must be NO subtitle under the brand, especially no "A headless agent..." descriptor.
Keep the exact large main headline "Adapt as fast as your market changes."
Replace the supporting paragraph with exactly:
"An agent that knows your business and uses market intelligence to spot risks and opportunities, coordinate a response and execute approved actions."
Preserve the green accent rule and benefit paragraph:
"Protect customer commitments.
Capture new demand. Keep teams aligned."
The hierarchy must read immediately: brand, customer promise, what the full agent does, business value. Headless is not part of this left hero.

2. RIGHT PRODUCT AND FULL LOOP.
Keep the large complete "Your next response is ready" panel and surrounding cycle from the original. Keep "Company brief", with three rows "What changed", "What it means for us", "Recommended response". Replace the majority of gray placeholder bars in those rows with meaningful short example text, using restrained small navy type:
"What changed": "Supply disruption and new demand"
"What it means for us": "Commitments to protect. An opportunity to qualify."
"Recommended response": "One plan across the business"
Four department columns "Procurement", "Operations", "Sales", "Finance", each with a short action:
"Secure supply", "Allocate stock", "Qualify demand", "Check costs".
Keep the prominent button "Review & approve".
Restore the surrounding original five-step cycle, with light mint arrows and simple line icons, all clearly visible:
"Know your business"
"Spot risks and opportunities"
"Coordinate the plan"
"Approve and act"
"Verify and adapt"
Under the cycle keep the original memory line "Company knowledge evolves with each decision".
The headless feature is complementary: add ONLY ONE small quiet secondary note inside the lower edge of the company brief or beside the action button, at ordinary caption size:
"Also acts through your existing tools."
Do not use a headless headline, headless brand descriptor, headless orbit or a second diagram. This note explains the additional ability to act through connected tools while preserving the complete product experience.

3. ACCEL FOOTER WITH UPDATED RECEIVED TARGET.
Retain the original clean three-column footer, fine vertical rules and uppercase small green headings.
"WHO IT'S FOR"
"Teams that buy, make, move and sell physical goods."
Smaller line "First: raw materials, timber, steel and construction materials."
"WHY NOW"
"Critical market information often arrives too late. Missing materials delay production, deliveries and construction projects."
"FIRST USERS"
"Targeted outreach to industrial operations and procurement leaders. Start with one critical supply workflow, then expand across sites and teams."

Keep the whole slide airy and readable. Do not add architecture panels, a working-core banner, sponsor names, numerical results, traction, a pricing panel, diagnostic/testing/synthetic-data language or demo labels. The image is a commercial product-vision proposal; do not invent a real connector result or execution receipt. Headless supports the product, it does not redefine it. The full original company-aware market-to-action loop and its prepared report must remain visually unmistakable.
